messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — infra perf alert from the nightly flashV2 run. mem-bandwidth shot up ~2.5x on long seqs (>=2048) after the fused-attn change. KV caching warming doesn't seem to lower the spike. attaching quick numbers below.

maria: Can you paste the perf counters and the exact binary/commit?

alex: commit 7a9f3e1 (flashv2-fuse). perf counters from the pinned machine: 
```
GPU: A100-sxm-40
batch=8, seq=2048, tokens/sec=12.3k -> dropped from 18.1k
DRAM BW: 780GB/s (peak)
SM Util: 63%
Shared Mem BW: 42%
KV cache hit rate: 71% (was 89% before)
```

sam: interesting — SM util down while DRAM BW up suggests tiling/pipeline shifted work into global mem. Did fuse remove an smem staging step?

li: infra-bot shows the deploy window: 
infra-bot: "deploy flashv2-fuse -> prod at 1765549800 (canary passed)"

alex: yeah fuse removed an explicit double-buffering stage to reduce latency, but it looks like we lost locality for paged-attn paths. paged prefetch is now firing later and causing lots of DRAM reads. KV pages being touched more often.

maria: can you repro with smaller seqs and vary tiling? maybe the tile size mapping changed. also try increasing pipeline stages back to 3.

alex: repro command I used: 
```bash
./bench_attn --model=gptx --kernel=flashv2_fuse --batch=8 --seq=2048 --kv-pages=64 --prefetch=1
```
changed prefetch to 2 reduced DRAM BW to ~520GB/s and restored tokens/sec to 16.5k. but latency tail got worse.

sam: hypothesis: the fused kernel reduced registers/shmem usage per warp which increased active warps -> but actually pipeline now stalls on global loads because prefetch window too small. occupancy tuning might help but we need to rebalance shmem vs registers.

li: can we run a micro-bench of just the attention macro-kernel with varied tile_x/tile_y to get bandwidth/latency surface? toss in CUPTI counters + nvprof flame.

maria: +1. Also please capture per-warp l1d stats, l2 miss ratio, and the KV touch pattern (hot vs cold pages). sample flame link: http://perf.internal/flames/1765551234 (private).

alex: will run. early results: increasing tile_x by 1 decreased l2 misses by 18% but increased shared mem usage to 92% -> occupancy dropped from 64% to 48% and throughput net neutral.

sam: that suggests a sweet spot tradeoff — we should add a kernel-selection rule: for seq >= 1536 prefer non-fused flashV2-paged with prefetch>=2, else fused for low-latency. add this to the runtime C++ policy table.

maria: also add a batching heuristic: detect long-seq-heavy traffic and lower microbatching to keep KV cache hot (e.g., dynamic microbatch cutoff at seq_len 1024 -> microbatch size 2).

li: i'll draft a short rollout plan: 1) revert to paged non-fused for canary 2) ship fused with updated prefetch=2 + tile tweak behind feature flag 3) add perf regression alert for DRAM BW > 60% of device peak for perf-run buckets.

alex: thanks. i'll attach raw traces and put the kernel micro-bench results in the perf board. want to avoid a silent cost regression in hosted customers.

maria: add an eval harness case that simulates KV-warm/cold transitions — that caught this earlier in prod.

sam: i'll own the runtime policy change and add a quick ablation test; ping me when traces are uploaded. :thumbsup:
